overall: The AG found the Everett School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law on notice, roll call, minutes, and records response, and the Search Committee violated it on minutes approval; intent was not found and several complaint-timeliness allegations were declined.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the January 11 executive session notice failed to identify the litigation matters or bargaining units to be discussed under Purpose 3.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find the January 11 notice and announcement insufficient with respect to all litigation matters discussed in executive session.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the January 18 executive session notice failed to identify the litigation matters or bargaining units to be discussed.
allegations.key_passage: However, the Committee failed to identify the third Open Meeting Law complainant whose complaint would be discussed and therefore we find that the notice and announcement were insufficient.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Committee did not take a roll call vote before convening in executive session on January 11.
allegations.key_passage: Finally, we find that the Committee failed to vote by roll call prior to entering executive session on January 11, in violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Not alleged in the complaint; the AG found the January 11 and 18 executive session minutes too vague to summarize the discussions and therefore inaccurate.
allegations.key_passage: Here, the minutes do not summarize the discussions that were held.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Committee failed to timely approve minutes of its December 20 and 27, 2023 meetings.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to timely approve the minutes of its December 20 and 27, 2023, meetings where those minutes were not approved until the

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Search Committee failed to timely approve several sets of its 2023 meeting minutes; the final three sets were found not untimely.
allegations.key_passage: Next, we find, and the Committee acknowledges, that the Search Committee violated the Open Meeting Law where it failed to timely approve several sets of meeting minutes.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Committee failed to timely respond to their January 2 request for meeting minutes.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee failed to timely respond to Attorney Fried's January 2 request for meeting minutes where it did not respond at all until after ten calendar days had passed.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Committee failed to timely review the executive session minutes it was asked to release in response to the January 2 request.
allegations.key_passage: the Committee was obligated to review the specific executive session minutes requested by its next meeting or 30 days, whichever was sooner.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged the Committee failed to timely respond to an Open Meeting Law complaint filed December 20, 2023.
allegations.key_passage: We find that the Committee failed to timely respond to the December 20, 2023, Open Meeting Law complaint where it did not respond until January 19, 2024, more than 14 business days after the complaint was filed with the Committee.

allegations.summary: Complainants alleged failure to timely respond to earlier OML complaints filed September 27 and December 8, 12, 13, 2023 by the Committee and Search Committee.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review this allegation with respect to the complaints filed on September 27 and December 8, 12, and 13, 2023, because the allegation is not timely with respect to these complaints.

allegations.summary: The second complaint alleged the Search Committee did not perform required steps before convening in executive session; the complainants acknowledged it was untimely.
allegations.key_passage: The second complaint also alleges that the Search Committee failed to perform the necessary steps prior to convening in executive session but acknowledges that this allegation is untimely.

allegations.summary: Complainant asked that the notice and roll-call violations be found intentional because the issue had been raised with the Committee more than once.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to find the violation to have been intentional.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
Amend the minutes of the January 11 and 18 executive sessions to summarize the discussions held.
Release the January 11 executive session minutes to the public, subject to permissible redactions.
Approve or ensure approval of the Search Committee minutes that have not yet been approved, including its final three meetings, within 45 days.
Review the executive session minutes requested on January 2 and respond by releasing any that may no longer be withheld and explaining any that remain withheld.
Certify compliance with the above to the AG within 45 days.
All Committee members to attend an Open Meeting Law webinar within 90 days of receipt and certify attendance within 95 days.
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution that future similar conduct may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.
